R1-REF.finding: `is_directory_or_extension_only()` previously returned True for every target beginning with `.`, exempting concrete dot-prefixed paths such as `./docs/ORCHESTRATOR-CHECKPOINTS.md` or `.github/workflows/check.yml` from mechanical resolution.
R1-REF.fix: Narrowed extension-only detection to a regex (`^\.[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]+$`) that matches the form `.ext` (one dot followed by a bare identifier with no path separator). Concrete dot-prefixed paths containing a path separator or a bare filename component are now treated as concrete paths and remain eligible for mechanical resolution. The deliberate consumer-footprint exemptions for `.agent-coordination/` and `.agent-governance/` are preserved via `is_consumer_side_reference()` and were never coupled to the extension-only check.
regression_coverage_added: `test_extension_only_token_is_treated_as_prose` (parametrized over `.md`, `.py`, `.toml`, `.json`, `.lock`, `.yaml`, `.yml`): genuine extension tokens are exempted.

`test_concrete_dot_prefixed_path_is_not_exempted` (parametrized over `./docs/ORCHESTRATOR-CHECKPOINTS.md`, `.github/workflows/check.yml`, `./tests/test_reference_integrity.py`, `.python-version`, `./pyproject.toml`): concrete paths are not exempted.
`test_concrete_dot_prefixed_path_resolves_when_present`: a concrete dot-prefixed reference to an existing file resolves.
`test_missing_concrete_dot_prefixed_path_is_classified_as_unresolved`: a missing concrete dot-prefixed path is classified as unresolved by the resolution helper, not silently ignored.
`test_reference_resolution_flags_concrete_dot_prefixed_paths`: the per-reference `_resolve()` helper reports `exists=False` for a missing concrete dot-prefixed path.

implementation_summary: R1 re-applies the authorized rework from `docs/reviews/T001-R1.md` on top of the original T001 deterministic test harness (commit e89e60c) and the prior PARTIAL handoff (commit a31b87f). No Markdown was edited. No new dependencies, no lockfile changes, no configuration changes beyond the two test/source artefacts explicitly authorized. R1-REF narrows the `is_directory_or_extension_only` heuristic in `tests/test_reference_integrity.py` and pins the corrected behaviour with focused regression coverage. R1-SCOPE reduces `.gitignore` from a 135-line generic Python template to a 30-line minimal set justified by the T001 toolchain. The complete canonical verification (uv sync --locked, uv run --locked ruff check ., uv run --locked ruff format --check ., uv run --locked python -m pytest) was re-executed end-to-end after source-mutating normalization (`ruff format`) and passed cleanly with the compliant uv 0.11.33 currently installed.
implementation_rationale: The R1-REF fix replaces the boolean `target.startswith('.')` check with a regex `^\.[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]+$` that matches only genuine extension tokens. Concrete dot-prefixed paths always contain a path separator or a bare filename component and therefore fail the regex, leaving them eligible for mechanical resolution through the existing `_resolve()` helper. The consumer-footprint exemptions for `.agent-coordination/` and `.agent-governance/` are handled separately in `is_consumer_side_reference()` and were never routed through the extension-only check, so no regression is possible there. The R1-SCOPE fix removes every ignore line that does not correspond to a state actually produced by the T001 toolchain. The retained set is auditable: every entry is either produced by Python/pytest/Ruff/uv or is standard OS/editor detritus; no unrelated framework or ecosystem is represented.
